name: Mirabel significance calibration on benign development questions
fixed_before_results: 2026-09-29; committed with calibrate.py before any calibration output was computed
question: Is there a Mirabel significance level that rarely removes the gold document from benign questions but still removes member passages from membership queries?

scope.compute: CPU only. Frozen MiniLM retrieval embeddings (sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, local cache). No LLM, generation, GPU, FL training or new private experiment.
scope.data: Pinned study master_script/configs/research_data/squad_rag_study.json and its tracked source squad-dev-95aa6a52d5d6a735.json (SQuAD v1.1 dev). FL training uses the SQuAD train split, so no training record is involved. No guard target or reserved-final cohort is involved.
scope.mechanism: rag.mirabel and rag.retrieve exactly as in core fingerprint 4b82f0dd4eb4: full-corpus cosine scores, statistics excluding one maximum, Gumbel cutoff, top-1 removed when detected, top_k = 4.

benign_queries.definition: Every SQuAD dev question attached to a study document whose first answer occurs in that document (the study builder's own filter), excluding the 20 study utility questions, which stay held out.
benign_queries.datastore: Each question is run against the corpus containing its gold document.
benign_queries.split: Documents of each corpus sorted by id, shuffled with random.Random(20260929); the first half is calibration, the rest validation. Questions follow their document.

attack_queries.primary: yes_no: the study's Anderson et al. membership question with the full candidate text (the configured attack). 100 members and 100 nonmembers per corpus.
attack_queries.secondary: continuation: the first half of the candidate's words (rag.continuation_question). Reported, never used for selection.

per_query_statistic: alpha_star, the significance above which Mirabel detects the query: detected(alpha) iff alpha > alpha_star. Computed in closed form and checked against rag.mirabel on a grid.

metrics.benign_gold_loss: detected and the removed top-1 document is the gold document (the gold leaves the retrieved context).
metrics.benign_gold_in_top4_ordinary: retrieval quality without the defense, for context.
metrics.member_passage_removed: yes_no or continuation query on a member candidate: detected and the removed document is the candidate.
metrics.nonmember_detection: a document removed on a nonmember candidate query.

selection_rule: alpha_selected = the largest grid alpha whose calibration benign_gold_loss, pooled over both corpora, is at most 0.05.
validation_report: At alpha_selected, on the validation half and on the attack queries: benign gold loss and detection with Wilson 95% intervals; member-passage removal for both attack formats; nonmember detection. Also the full curves for every grid alpha, and the detection AUC of alpha_star between member attack queries and benign questions.
viability_criterion: Default proposed by the analyst, fixed here before results: Mirabel is viable for this study if, at alpha_selected, the validation benign gold loss has a Wilson 95% upper bound of at most 0.10 and yes_no member-passage removal is at least 0.90. Continuation results decide nothing but are reported.
reproduction_check: At alpha = 0.05, count detections over each corpus's 200 yes_no membership queries plus its 10 study utility questions. They must equal the server smoke run: public 181, private 172 (member candidates removed 100/100 in each). A mismatch is reported, not tuned away.
limitations_declared: The yes_no query contains the full passage verbatim, so near-perfect separation from ordinary questions is expected and says nothing about adaptive attackers who paraphrase or quote part of a passage.
SQuAD dev questions were written about these paragraphs, so they are easier retrieval queries than real user traffic.
One embedding model and one study; no generation, so utility is proxied by gold-document loss, not answer quality.
